clue.text: Bet many got frozen

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
frozen means iced, chilled solid

explanation.surface: A big wager and plenty of people left cold with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bet' is a verb here: to dice is to gamble with dice.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice is to gamble at dice, so having diced means having wagered.

clue.text: Special military unit displays aloofness

explanation.surface: A crack squad shows coldness.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of troops sent on special duty; also emotional distance and indifference.

clue.text: Take crack before gin? Rubbish!

indicators.note: before puts the crack ahead of the gin

parts.note: a crack of thunder is a clap
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone takes a swig of gin and scoffs at nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare, as in a gin trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious nonsense or empty talk, i.e. drivel.

clue.text: Extent to which diets can be adapted

indicators.note: be adapted says these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: Asking how far eating plans may be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the length or span between points, its reach.

clue.text: Fatty fare first offered to Fischer-Dieskau

indicators.note: first says the word for fare comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: fare is food, a diet
fatty food is rich

explanation.surface: Greasy food is the first thing served to a famous German baritone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the forename given to the baritone Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau; 'first' puts the fare before the fatty.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer's given name, the one bestowed on him before his surname.

clue.text: Spring flower in the South-West

explanation.surface: A seasonal bloom in a part of England.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows: the River Dart runs through Devon in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to leap or dash; the Dart is a river in Devon.

clue.text: Part of the oath I eventually had to take

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone swears an oath and finally feels compelled to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to steal, i.e. take what is not yours.

clue.text: Serial produced in the country

indicators.note: produced says the letters are made into something different

explanation.surface: A drama series is filmed abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a Middle Eastern nation.

clue.text: Cease walking if lame

explanation.surface: Stop moving if injured.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop walking; halt is also an old word for limping or crippled.

clue.text: Trucker treats me awfully badly

indicators.note: awfully badly says these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A lorry driver complains of being treated terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a teamster is a lorry driver, a member of the truckers' union.

clue.text: Do leave the rest to participate!

explanation.surface: An order to stop resting and join in.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, to take a part is to have one piece and leave the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one share and leaving the remainder; also to join in an activity.

clue.text: Foolishly enrage GI by giving consent

indicators.note: foolishly says these letters are put together in a silly new order

explanation.surface: A soldier is unwisely angered by saying yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing means assenting, saying yes to something.

clue.text: Its blade could injure a girl

definitions.text: Its blade could injure a girl

parts.note: to injure with an edge is to cut
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A sharp weapon that might wound a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved sword with a single cutting edge, as used by sailors.

clue.text: Vandals think it's wonderful

parts.note: the word for wonderful is also what vandals do to windows, breaking things

explanation.surface: Hooligans enjoy wrecking things.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British slang for excellent, and literally breaking things to pieces.

clue.text: Wondered why Restoration poet had little education

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English poet active at the Restoration
ED is a short form of education

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why a seventeenth-century poet was poorly schooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Marvelled means was amazed, so it is synonymous with wondered.

clue.text: The visionary who takes a siesta

explanation.surface: An idealist naps in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in fanciful thoughts; literally one dreaming during the day, as at a nap.

clue.text: Fast-talking results in rapid postal service

explanation.surface: Talking quickly produces speedy mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: a delivery of words that is express, or fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech given at speed; also a premium mail service for quick dispatch.

clue.text: One allowed to support Redcaps without reservation

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means to sit underneath the other piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Redcaps are British military police, abbreviated MP
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: A permitted man backs the military police wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit faith or trust is absolute and unquestioning.

clue.text: Once last month a social worker was elated

parts.note: ex means former, once
ult, short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A former colleague was thrilled about something last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a carer, but it is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Exultant means jubilant, triumphantly happy.

clue.text: A playwright resettling at Reading

indicators.note: resettling says the letters are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dramatist moves house to a town in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading, capitalised to look like the Berkshire town, is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a writer of tragedies, so a kind of dramatist.

clue.text: Counsel discloses commercial malpractice

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
vice is wrongdoing, malpractice

explanation.surface: A barrister uncovers advertising fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel as a noun means guidance or recommendations.

clue.text: E rushed into the road to do this job

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
rushed means ran

explanation.surface: Someone called E dashed into the street to do a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to carry out a task, such as shopping.

clue.text: Society girl and I shelter in 6

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for a girl
lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A debutante and I take cover somewhere in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer of 6 down, ISRAEL; the definition names a region found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around the Sea of Galilee lies in northern Israel.

clue.text: Publicity causing a fellow to fume

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow
to fume is to rage

explanation.surface: Media attention makes a man seethe.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage is the reporting and attention a story receives.

clue.text: A GP returned for the finale

indicators.note: returned says the letters are read back to front

parts.note: a GP, a general practitioner, is a doc

explanation.surface: A family doctor came back for the closing act.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Fencers use it to score record points

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
E and E are compass points, east twice

explanation.surface: Swordsmen employ this to win hits.
explanation.definitionFit: The epee is a fencing sword.

clue.text: Broadcast supporting wage demand

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
a pay claim is a demand for higher wages

explanation.surface: A union announces backing for a pay demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to announce it publicly, to declare it.

clue.text: Entertaining tale made deacon take note

indicators.note: made says the letters are worked into something new

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A churchman is forced to write something down.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusing short story about a real incident.

clue.text: Old Mongolian thanks Jack

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
jack and tar are both words for a sailor

explanation.surface: An ancient horseman expresses gratitude to a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars were a historic Mongolic people of the steppes.
